title: Recurring schedules missed during downtime fire once per poll cycle instead of collapsing to the next future occurrence
userUtcOffsetMinutes is accepted but never applied; all parsed times are computed in UTC
Weekly dayOfWeek and monthly dayOfMonth are ignored when advancing the next occurrence
body:
## Description

`RecurrenceRule` carries `dayOfWeek` for weekly rules and `dayOfMonth` for monthly rules (`packages/intelligence/src/schedule-parser.ts:14-19`), but `_nextOccurrence` ignores both fields and simply adds a fixed offset to the previous trigger:

```ts
// packages/intelligence/src/schedule-store.ts:296-305
switch (rule.kind) {
  case "weekly":
    d.setUTCDate(d.getUTCDate() + rule.intervalWeeks * 7);
    break;
  case "monthly":
    d.setUTCMonth(d.getUTCMonth() + 1);
    break;
```

For weekly rules the anchor weekday is whatever weekday the first `triggerAt` happened to fall on; `rule.dayOfWeek` is never consulted. For monthly rules the day-of-month is whatever the first trigger's day was, and `setUTCMonth(+1)` additionally rolls over on short months (e.g. advancing from Jan 31 lands in early March), so `rule.dayOfMonth` is neither honoured nor stable.

## Impact

A reminder intended for "every Monday" or "the 1st of every month" recurs on the wrong day whenever the requested day differs from the first occurrence's day, or drifts across month boundaries. Recurring reminders silently fire on incorrect dates. Rated medium: it degrades the correctness of recurring schedules but does not crash or lose data, and the parser does not yet populate these fields for most phrasings (limiting current blast radius).

## Required Fix

1. In the `weekly` branch, after adding `intervalWeeks * 7` days, snap the result to `rule.dayOfWeek` when defined.
2. In the `monthly` branch, clamp to `rule.dayOfMonth` (capped to the target month's length) instead of carrying the original day, and avoid `setUTCMonth` rollover by setting the date explicitly.
3. Add tests covering weekly `dayOfWeek` selection and monthly `dayOfMonth` on short months (e.g. Jan 31 monthly should not skip February).

## References

- Rule shape: `packages/intelligence/src/schedule-parser.ts:14-19`.

title: CacheKeyGenerator store is unbounded and performs an O(n) embedding scan on every lookup
AlertRouter.alertHistory grows without bound
body:
## Description

`AlertRouter` retains every alert it ever sees in an in-memory array that is only ever appended to:

```ts
// packages/intelligence/src/alert-router.ts:38
private readonly alertHistory: Alert[] = [];
```

Both the suppressed path and the dispatched path push, and nothing trims the array:

```ts
// packages/intelligence/src/alert-router.ts:67-78
if (suppressedUntil > full.detectedAt) {
  full.suppressedUntil = suppressedUntil;
  this.alertHistory.push(full);   // suppressed alerts retained too
  return full;
}
...
this.alertHistory.push(full);     // dispatched alerts retained
```

There is no maximum size, ring buffer, or pruning anywhere in the class; `getHistory()` copies and reverses the whole array on each call.

## Impact

In a long-running process every emitted alert — including deduplicated/suppressed ones — is held forever, so memory grows monotonically with alert volume, and `getHistory()` cost grows linearly with the total. The anomaly detector calls `alertRouter.emit` on each detected anomaly (`packages/intelligence/src/anomaly-detector.ts:106-112`), so a noisy metric stream steadily accumulates `Alert` objects. Rated medium: a slow but unbounded leak in an always-on subsystem; it will eventually pressure memory but does not cause immediate failure.

## Required Fix

1. Cap `alertHistory` to a configurable maximum (e.g. a ring buffer or shift-on-overflow), defaulting to a sane bound.
2. Expose the retention size via `AlertRouterConfig` alongside the existing `deduplicationWindowMs`.
3. Make `getHistory(limit?)` slice rather than copy-and-reverse the entire array.

## References

- Emit call site: `packages/intelligence/src/anomaly-detector.ts:106-112`.
- CWE-401: Missing Release of Memory after Effective Lifetime.

title: Anomaly alert threshold always reports the upper z-score bound, mislabeling low-side anomalies
body:
## Description

Detection is correctly two-sided — z-score uses `Math.abs(...)` and the IQR fence checks both ends (`packages/intelligence/src/anomaly-detector.ts:76-85`):

```ts
const iqrAnomaly =
  (this.method === "iqr" || this.method === "both") &&
  baseline.iqr > 0 &&
  (value > baseline.q3 + this.iqrMultiplier * baseline.iqr ||
    value < baseline.q1 - this.iqrMultiplier * baseline.iqr);
```

But the `threshold` reported on the emitted alert is hard-coded to the **upper** z-score bound regardless of which side tripped (`packages/intelligence/src/anomaly-detector.ts:106-112`):

```ts
const alert = await this.alertRouter.emit({
  metric,
  severity,
  ...
  value,
  threshold: baseline.mean + this.zScoreThreshold * baseline.stdDev,
});
```

For a low-side anomaly (value far below the mean, or below the lower IQR fence), the alert advertises an upper threshold the value never exceeded, and for an IQR-only detection it reports a z-score-derived bound unrelated to the fence that actually fired.

## Impact

Downstream consumers of `Alert.threshold` (dashboards, handlers, the `markFalsePositive` feedback loop) receive a meaningless or misleading bound for low-side and IQR-detected anomalies — e.g. a value of 2 flagged as anomalously low against a mean of 100 is reported with `threshold` ≈ `mean + 3σ`, implying it was too *high*. Detection still works; the reported context is wrong. Rated medium: misleading alert metadata that can cause incorrect triage, but not a missed detection.

## Required Fix

1. Choose the threshold on the side the value actually violated: for z-score, use `mean - zσ` when `value < mean`, else `mean + zσ`.
2. When the anomaly was detected by IQR, report the IQR fence (`q1 - k*iqr` or `q3 + k*iqr`) that was crossed instead of a z-score bound.
3. Add tests asserting the reported `threshold` matches the violated bound for low-side and IQR-only cases.

## References

- Alert shape: `packages/intelligence/src/alert-router.ts:9-19`.

title: "every 0 days"/"every 0 weeks" is accepted and produces a non-advancing schedule that re-fires every poll
ScheduleParser confidence penalty for missing intent is dead code
Bare/"next" weekday resolution always skips the current day even when the requested time is still ahead
UNIT_MS approximates month and year as fixed 30/365 days, causing date drift
body:
## Description

Relative "in N months/years" expressions are computed by adding a fixed millisecond constant rather than using calendar arithmetic:

```ts
// packages/intelligence/src/time-parser.ts:51-59
const UNIT_MS: Record<string, number> = {
  second: 1_000,
  minute: 60_000,
  hour: 3_600_000,
  day: 86_400_000,
  week: 7 * 86_400_000,
  month: 30 * 86_400_000,   // every month treated as exactly 30 days
  year: 365 * 86_400_000,   // every year treated as exactly 365 days
};
```

This table is used for the "in N unit(s)" and "N unit(s) ago" branches (`packages/intelligence/src/time-parser.ts:153,163`), so "in 1 month" is always now + 30 days and "in 1 year" is now + 365 days.

## Impact

"In 1 month" lands on the wrong calendar day for any month that is not 30 days (off by 1–2 days for 28/29/31-day months), and "in 1 year" is off by a day across leap years; errors accumulate for larger N. Reminders set with month/year granularity drift from the user's intent. Rated low: small, bounded drift on coarse-grained relative expressions; sub-month units are exact.

## Required Fix

1. Handle `month` and `year` with calendar arithmetic (`setUTCMonth(+n)` / `setUTCFullYear(+n)`) instead of fixed-ms multiplication, clamping day-of-month for short months.
2. Keep the fixed-ms path for second/minute/hour/day/week, and add tests for "in 1 month" across 28/31-day months and "in 1 year" across a leap year.

## References

None.

title: Baseline stdDev uses population variance (÷n) instead of sample variance (÷n−1)
body:
## Description

`getBaseline` divides the summed squared deviations by `n`, computing the population variance, even though the window is a finite *sample* of an ongoing stream used to estimate the underlying distribution:

```ts
// packages/intelligence/src/baseline-profiler.ts:71-73
const mean = sorted.reduce((s, v) => s + v, 0) / n;
const variance = sorted.reduce((s, v) => s + (v - mean) ** 2, 0) / n;
const stdDev = Math.sqrt(variance);
```

For sample-based estimation the unbiased estimator divides by `n - 1` (Bessel's correction). The function already guards `n >= 2` (`packages/intelligence/src/baseline-profiler.ts:66`), so `n - 1` is safe.

## Impact

The reported `stdDev` is biased slightly low, which in turn feeds the anomaly detector's z-score test and severity classification (`packages/intelligence/src/anomaly-detector.ts:79,103-104`). The bias is most pronounced for small windows and makes the detector marginally more sensitive (lower effective threshold). Rated low: a small statistical bias that shrinks as the window fills, not a functional break.

## Required Fix

1. Divide by `n - 1` to use the unbiased sample variance, or expose a config flag if population variance is intentionally desired for some callers.
2. Update/extend tests to lock in the chosen estimator.

## References

- Consumer: `packages/intelligence/src/anomaly-detector.ts:79,103-104`.
